title: A lone odd loop shields the transverse twist
subject: Whether the probability of a lone odd contradiction loop along a class depends on how the transverse direction is twisted
conclusion: On every square-lattice torus, at every shear and for every primitive class c, the two twists odd on c give exactly the same probability that the twisted strong components wind along c and nothing else, for fair orientations. An explicit involution proves it: sliding the second twist's seam onto the upper boundary of the odd loop, with bit flips on edges entered from the free side, changes no directed cycle.
